ai.description: *Megophrys periosa* reaches 12–14 cm. It is brown with dark dorsal markings and a pale throat. Key features include prominent "horns" above the eyes and a distinct, fleshy rostral appendage.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys periosa* is best distinguished by its exceptionally large, prominent "horns" (elongated, triangular upper eyelids) that are significantly longer than other Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Megophrys periosa* inhabits dense, humid evergreen forests and mountain streams in the Eastern Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Giant Himalayan Horned Frog is a master of camouflage, remaining motionless on the forest floor to ambush passing prey while blending perfectly with leaf litter.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys periosa* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in mountain streams. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys periosa* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically across Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, at elevations ranging from approximately 1,000 to 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Giant Himalayan Horned Frog emits a loud, explosive "cluck" or "bonk" sound at a low pitch, typically heard echoing near fast-flowing mountain streams in dense forests.
